in_sanskrit.name: जयामिनी
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: जय (Jaya) meaning victory or triumph + आमिनी (Amini) meaning prosperous or wealth. Thus, Jayaamini means 'Victorious and Prosperous' or 'Triumphant and Wealthy'.

data.cultural_impact: Jayaamini is a revered name in Hinduism, particularly in Tamil Nadu and other regions of South India. The name embodies the spirit of triumph and victory, inspiring courage and determination among its bearers and those who revere it. It is not uncommon for individuals to be named Jayaamini as a wish for their success and happiness in all aspects of life.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jayaamini holds deep spiritual significance for Hindus. It represents the idea that victory comes from within, from the strength and determination of the individual. The name is a reminder that Goddess Jayaamini is always by their side, offering her blessings and guidance. It is a name that instills a sense of devotion and dedication, encouraging those who bear it to strive for excellence in all aspects of their lives, while always remaining humble and grateful for the divine blessings bestowed upon them.

historical_references.reference: Jayaamini was a famous Tamil poetess and a queen consort of the Chola Emperor Rajaraja I (r. 985-1014 AD). She was also known by the name Kundavai. Her poems, known as Agam Tirumurai, are considered to be an important work in the Tamil literary tradition.
historical_references.context: Chola Empire, Tamil poetess and queen consort of Emperor Rajaraja I, author of Agam Tirumurai.

historical_references.reference: Jaya Devi or Jayaamini was a princess of the Eastern Chalukya Dynasty who married the Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana in 1118 AD. This marked the beginning of the Hoysala Empire's dominance over the Deccan region. Jaya Devi is also known for her role in the Changama Mahotsavam festival.
historical_references.context: Eastern Chalukya Dynasty, Hoysala Empire, princess and queen consort of King Vishnuvardhana, role in Changama Mahotsavam festival.
